source.title: Certified Interventional Fidelity: Anytime-Valid, Adaptive Evaluation of Causal Claims in Mechanistic Interpretability

page_placements.theme: Mediation concentrates in middle-to-late layers under specified interventions

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates GPT-2 Small IOI circuits with clean-to-corrupted activation patching and a normalized recovery measure, rather than applying the original circuit’s full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2 IOI results report patching recovery for five circuit sizes. CIF certification stopping times are not separate behavioral results. The sensitivity results in E3 concern MNIST abstractions, not GPT-2 IOI, so they are not recorded as rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper is a statistical method (anytime-valid confidence sequences) and uses GPT-2 Small IOI circuits as a test bed. Its IOI results are recovery estimates and certification costs for 3–13-head circuits. The text never says which circuit came from which method (ACDC, attribution patching, AtP*, hand-identified). None is the 26-head, 7-class circuit, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not assessed. The results show how CIF performs, not whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CIF certifies high patching recovery (µ ≥ 0.90, and ≥ 0.95 for the larger circuits) for GPT-2 Small IOI circuits. Betting confidence sequences need about 10–30× fewer samples than Hoeffding bounds. They present diminishing returns after the name-mover heads only as a suggestion, based on lower confidence bounds of 0.953–0.966. They make no claim about whether the IOI circuit itself is correct.
record.recipe_differences: Uses clean-to-corrupted activation patching, but evaluates clipped normalized recovery with confidence sequences rather than applying the original circuit's full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: In the MNIST abstraction experiment, conclusions vary with intervention distribution and discrepancy metric: at p ≤ 0.2 the metric confidence sequences overlap, while at p = 0.5 the reported 0–1-loss and clipped-KL fidelity estimates differ and their intervals do not overlap. These sensitivity results are not for GPT-2 IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: Restoring 3–13 attention heads from clean into corrupted IOI prompts recovers about 96–97% of the clipped logit-difference gap (µ̂ 0.959–0.972). Gains beyond the core name-mover heads are small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of IOI heads, starting with the name movers, suffices to restore most of the clean IOI logit difference under activation patching in GPT-2 Small.

record.problems: The IOI results do not map each evaluated circuit size to a discovery method, and the paper does not provide the prompt distribution or individual confidence interval endpoints. Patching recovery does not establish the exact 26-head, 7-class circuit or its full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant GPT-2 IOI patching-recovery results were left out. CIF stopping-time results are mentioned in notes rather than treated as separate behavioral rows; MNIST abstraction results are outside the GPT-2 IOI claim.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit, head roles, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not evaluated.
Backup name-mover takeover after ablation is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse are not tested.
Circuits from ACDC, attribution patching and AtP* are evaluated, but they are not mapped to sizes and not compared for overlap. Ablation types and metrics are not varied for IOI.
Sensitivity to ablation, metric and distribution (E3) is reported only for MNIST abstractions, not for GPT-2 IOI.
Name orders, templates and prompts with more names are not evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's label (V1 supports) is dropped: the evaluated circuits are unidentified 3–13-head sets, not the 26-head circuit. The paper does not link circuit sizes to discovery methods, and gives no corruption scheme or prompt distribution. The E3 sensitivity results are on MNIST only. Results are uniform and from a single-author preprint; code is released.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish the exact 26-head, 7-class circuit or test the stated roles of its head classes, nor does it apply the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria or test removal of everything outside that circuit.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and component reuse across tasks are not tested.
The study evaluates circuits proposed by several methods but does not compare whether they recover essentially the same circuit, or compare ablation types and metrics for that purpose.

Sensitivity of GPT-2 IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric, or prompt distribution, and whether the circuit explains only part of IOI behavior, are not tested. The paper's sensitivity experiment is on MNIST abstractions.
Alternative name orders, templates, and prompts with more names are not evaluated.

relation.reason: The study uses existing IOI circuits to demonstrate CIF without a result resolving any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: IOI circuits serve as a test bed for confidence-sequence precision and certification cost. The reported recovery estimates do not establish the specified circuit composition, completeness, minimality, backup behavior, or mechanism invariance.

source_check.notes: Recovery is the mean of per-prompt clipped normalized logit-difference recovery. Discovery methods are named but not mapped to circuit sizes; head identities, corruption scheme, and prompt distribution are unspecified.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The five GPT-2 Small circuit sizes evaluated with clean-to-corrupted IOI patching
reader_labels.reason: All reported circuits have high normalized recovery estimates (0.959–0.972), supporting strong patch recovery in these tested settings; see r1–r5.
